`export async function turn(sessionId: string | undefined, message: string): Promise<{ reply: string; sessionId: string }>`
With `undefined` it starts a new conversation. An id that an earlier call returned continues that conversation, even from a new process. The Gemini API key is in the `GEMINI_API_KEY` environment variable.

These are just my test session's leftover snapshot files (not the app's own data), so I'll remove them entirely since the directory would otherwise only exist from my manual test.

`src/index.ts` now exports `turn(sessionId, message)` instead of `reply`. It uses Genkit's beta agent API (`ai.defineAgent` + `FileSessionStore`) to persist conversation snapshots to `./.genkit/sessions`, so passing `undefined` starts a new conversation and passing back a returned `sessionId` resumes it — verified across separate `tsx` process invocations that it actually remembers context after a restart.
